transcript.content: Hi, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, well, I guess I'm here because... well, I hope it's okay to just jump right into it. Things have just been a little stressful lately regarding my father's passing. 

I mean, I know everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and the, um, the donation emails all line up perfectly. And I really don't want to sound unreasonable or difficult, I promise I'm looking at this logically since I work with data all day as a systems analyst. But... well, when I actually compare the timestamps on the files, and I see these missing attachments, and then I notice the way certain community members completely avoid my questions when I bring it up... it just, it seems obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right and giving you what you need.
Do you believe for certain that people are hiding the truth about your father's death?

Um... "for certain" is... well, it's a strong way to put it, and I really don't want to come across as, you know, paranoid or difficult. I know how people view this kind of thing, and I really want to be reasonable about it. 

But... yes. I mean, when you just look at the raw data—the timestamps that don't match up, the attachments that are just gone—it just doesn't add up any other way. And when I try to just have a polite conversation about it with people in the community, they completely shut down or avoid me. So, logically... yes, I do believe someone is hiding what actually happened. 

I hope I'm not sounding too... out there. I just want to make sure I'm giving you honest answers. Is this the kind of information you need?
Is it possible, in your mind, that you could be mistaken about people hiding the truth about your father's death?

I... I really want to say yes. I'd love to just agree and say I'm mistaken, because I know that would make things so much easier for everyone, and I really hate causing any kind of friction. I try so hard to look at my own biases, I promise I do. 

But... well, like I was saying, when I sit down and actually look at the hospital records and the donation emails... I know everyone keeps telling me they line up perfectly, but they just don't. The missing attachments, the timestamps being altered... data doesn't lie. And when people in the community literally turn and walk away or change the subject when I ask a polite question about it... I just can't see how I could be wrong. It's just too obvious to me that someone is hiding the real story about his passing. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not what you want to hear, and I really don't want to sound stubborn or obsessive. Am I being too difficult about this? I just want to make sure I'm being totally honest with you so you can do your job.
Aside from your father's death, do you believe anyone is hiding things from you or conspiring against you in other parts of your life?

Oh, no, no, not at all. Um, I really hope I haven't given the impression that I think everyone is out to get me or anything like that. I know how that sounds, and I promise I'm not... I'm not paranoid about everything. 

My work is fine, my friends are great. It's really just... just this one specific thing with my dad's records. Everything else in my life is completely normal, I swear. I try really hard to be easy to work with and get along with people. I don't think there's any big conspiracy against me personally. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering you clearly and not making things seem worse than they are. I'm doing okay otherwise, really.
How long have you believed that someone is hiding the truth about your father's death?

Um... I guess it's been about nine months now. It really started in the period right after he passed away, when I first had to sit down and start sorting through his records and his messages to get his estate in order. 

I know nine months probably sounds like a really long time to be focused on something like this, and I really hope you don't think I'm just obsessing over it or unable to move on. I was just trying to do the right thing and handle his affairs properly, like anyone would, and that's just when I noticed the data didn't match up. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right timeline for your notes, I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Has this belief caused serious problems in your daily life?

Oh, um, no. No, not serious problems at all, really. I mean, I still go to work every day, I handle all my systems analysis projects just fine, I pay my bills... my normal routine is completely intact. I try really hard to make sure it doesn't spill over into my day-to-day responsibilities, you know? 

I guess... well, the only place things get a little tense is sometimes when I bring up my questions about the records with my family, or with some of the people in the community. I know it can be uncomfortable for them, and I really hate causing any friction, so I try not to push too hard. But as far as my actual life goes, I'm functioning perfectly fine. 

Is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture. I don't want you to think my life is falling apart or anything, because it's really not.
